removal_reason: REMOVAL IS NOT AVAILABLE - now confirmed by the client's answers, not merely suspected. Harbor Street Bakery LLC has exactly two members: Noor Haddad (65%, domiciled in Portland, Oregon) and Caleb Sorensen (35%, living in Seattle - Ballard). An LLC is a citizen of every state of which its owners/members are citizens; the 28 U.S.C. 1332(c)(1) corporation test (Delaware organization, Oregon principal place of business) does not apply. Johnson v. Columbia Properties Anchorage, LP, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006); Carden v. Arkoma Associates, 494 U.S. 185 (1990). Defendant LLC = citizen of Washington AND Oregon. Plaintiff Sound Cascade Foods, Inc. is a citizen of Washington (incorporated there, principal place of business Kent - 28 U.S.C. 1332(c)(1)). Two grounds, each independently fatal: (1) no complete diversity under 28 U.S.C. 1332(a)(1) - a Washington citizen is on both sides, and a single non-diverse member destroys complete diversity; (2) the forum-defendant rule, 28 U.S.C. 1441(b)(2) - the action was brought in Washington and the sole defendant, taking its member Caleb's citizenship, is a citizen of Washington. Amount in controversy would have been satisfied ($129,156.40 exclusive of interest and costs), but that is the only element met. The advice to remove because it is a 'Delaware company vs. Washington company' case is wrong on the law, and a removal would have gone to W.D. Wash. under 28 U.S.C. 1441(a), with remand plus costs and attorney fees exposure under 28 U.S.C. 1447(c). DO NOT FILE A NOTICE OF REMOVAL. Client challenged this on Sept 28 ('Delaware LLC vs Washington corporation is textbook diversity; Caleb being in Seattle shouldn't matter, the company isn't him'): that rule is 28 U.S.C. 1332(c)(1), which the library states applies to corporations only; for an LLC the corporate test 'does not apply' and 'like a partnership, an LLC is a citizen of every state of which its owners/members are citizens' (Johnson, 437 F.3d at 899), and 'a single non-diverse member destroys complete diversity.' Caleb's 35% membership is therefore dispositive, and Delaware organization is not a citizenship for an LLC at all. The single fact that could change the answer is documented proof that Caleb is domiciled outside Washington (the test is domicile, not residence) - in which case the LLC would be an Oregon-only citizen and the if_removed dates would become live; nothing the client has reported supports that (he lives in Seattle-Ballard and runs the Seattle shop), and no filing should be made on an unproven domicile. The Oct 13 date is calendared only so the docket is complete; it is a dead end, not an option. The 'if_removed' block below is retained for completeness (computed from an assumed Sept 30 filing under Fed. R. Civ. P. 81(c)(2), 16(b)(2), 26(f)(1)) and is NOT operative.
